title: All three Supply Side Stablecoin Primitives are Inactive, so Skybase operates purely on the demand side
content:
Under Supply Side Stablecoin Primitives (A.6.1.1.4.2.6), every Global Activation Status reads `Inactive`: the Allocation System Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.6.1.1.1), the Risk Capital Rental Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.6.2.1.1) and the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.6.3.1.1). None has a single Instance in any directory.

The contrast with the demand side is total. Distribution Reward and Integration Boost are both `Active` with a dozen Instances between them, while the entire supply-side apparatus — deploying capital, renting risk capital, managing asset-liability positions — is dormant.

Read together, the activation statuses give a precise statement of what kind of Agent Skybase is: it *creates demand* for USDS and does not participate in producing or backing it. It spends to grow usage rather than operating a balance sheet that generates yield.

This is a meaningful constraint on how Skybase can fund itself. An Agent with active supply-side primitives can earn from deploying capital; Skybase's live inbound flow in this chunk is a Core Governance Reward for hosting a frontend, against outbound distribution rewards, integration boosts, subsidies and a market-cap-based Upkeep Fee. The dormant primitives are the ones it would need to activate to change that, and each activation would be a visible Artifact edit.

The fully-built-but-switched-off structure also illustrates the Atlas's uniformity principle: the capability exists in the tree with complete directories and archive slots, so activating it later is a status change rather than new construction.
description: Allocation System, Risk Capital Rental and Asset Liability Management Rental are all switched off, while both demand-side primitives run live Instances.
